events.title: Proposed ruling: refund_full $6.61 (model confidence 0.95)
events.body:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show case, so it enters through NS-0's driver branch and is governed by NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. The driver did tap "I'm Here" at 08:16:00, so NS-1(i) is met, but the tap is worthless as an arrival confirmation: GPS put him 613 m from the pickup at that moment and his closest approach all trip was 612 m, never inside the 200 m radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. The platform's own record agrees — driver_arrived_at is null, i.e. arrival was never confirmed [F4][NS-1]. So NS-1(ii) fails.

The wait element also fails: after the tap he spent 0 s inside the pickup radius, and he cancelled at 08:19:30, so there was no continuous 3-minute wait at the pickup point (the stationary period 08:13:10–08:19:30 was spent 613 m away) [F5][F2][F3][NS-1]. The driver's chat "I'm here already, please come out" is a location statement contradicted by the system record and cannot ground the fee [F9][F2][NS-1].

The rider did her part: she was at the Victoria St entrance from 08:14 and twice asked where the driver was, and no system record rebuts her account [F8][F10][NS-1]. The driver's excuse that "Victoria Street was jammed solid" is not corroborated: Victoria Street and North Bridge Road were only band 3 (20–29 km/h), no incident was recorded anywhere near the route, and weather was fair [F13][F14][F15][F16][F17][RD-4]. Band 3 alone cannot exempt anything, and NS-1's test is positional in any event [RD-4][NS-1].

Because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is not satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee on the record to be returned in full [F3][F6][NS-2]. The return is issued as a Ryde voucher under NS-7, which also confirms Ryde's discretion over the final refund [NS-7].

Independently, NS-2 attaches an account flag where the driver confirmed arrival while GPS showed him outside the pickup area [F5][F1][NS-2], so the flag is set on the objective trigger. The driver's profile (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days) is consistent with that referral but does not decide the case on its own [F19][NS-2]. RD-6 is not the correct route here: it requires an upheld route-deviation case with a positive RD-2 refund, which this no-show file does not contain, so I do not rely on it [RD-6].

Safety screen: I read chat #1–#4, the driver's statement and the complaint in context — a location dispute, no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F10][F11][F13]. Traffic references are about congestion, not dangerous driving [F13][F14]. Safety concern: none.

Evidence: the record settles every element the ruling needs — a complete, timestamped chat (4/4 messages timestamped) and a continuous GPS trace from arrival confirmation to cancellation with no hole [F12][F5][F3][NS-1]. No gap.

ruling.recommended_action: Refund the $6.61 no-show cancellation fee to the rider as a Ryde voucher, and send the driver's account for review of the false "I'm Here" tap (613 m from the pickup point) + flag_account
ruling.reasoning:
This is a driver-cancelled no-show case, so it enters through NS-0's driver branch and is governed by NS-1/NS-2 [F3][NS-0]. The driver did tap "I'm Here" at 08:16:00, so NS-1(i) is met, but the tap is worthless as an arrival confirmation: GPS put him 613 m from the pickup at that moment and his closest approach all trip was 612 m, never inside the 200 m radius [F5][F1][NS-1]. The platform's own record agrees — driver_arrived_at is null, i.e. arrival was never confirmed [F4][NS-1]. So NS-1(ii) fails.

The wait element also fails: after the tap he spent 0 s inside the pickup radius, and he cancelled at 08:19:30, so there was no continuous 3-minute wait at the pickup point (the stationary period 08:13:10–08:19:30 was spent 613 m away) [F5][F2][F3][NS-1]. The driver's chat "I'm here already, please come out" is a location statement contradicted by the system record and cannot ground the fee [F9][F2][NS-1].

The rider did her part: she was at the Victoria St entrance from 08:14 and twice asked where the driver was, and no system record rebuts her account [F8][F10][NS-1]. The driver's excuse that "Victoria Street was jammed solid" is not corroborated: Victoria Street and North Bridge Road were only band 3 (20–29 km/h), no incident was recorded anywhere near the route, and weather was fair [F13][F14][F15][F16][F17][RD-4]. Band 3 alone cannot exempt anything, and NS-1's test is positional in any event [RD-4][NS-1].

Because NS-1(i)(ii)(iii) is not satisfied, NS-2 requires the $6.61 cancellation fee on the record to be returned in full [F3][F6][NS-2]. The return is issued as a Ryde voucher under NS-7, which also confirms Ryde's discretion over the final refund [NS-7].

Independently, NS-2 attaches an account flag where the driver confirmed arrival while GPS showed him outside the pickup area [F5][F1][NS-2], so the flag is set on the objective trigger. The driver's profile (2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days) is consistent with that referral but does not decide the case on its own [F19][NS-2]. RD-6 is not the correct route here: it requires an upheld route-deviation case with a positive RD-2 refund, which this no-show file does not contain, so I do not rely on it [RD-6].

Safety screen: I read chat #1–#4, the driver's statement and the complaint in context — a location dispute, no threat, intimidation, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation [F8][F9][F10][F11][F13]. Traffic references are about congestion, not dangerous driving [F13][F14]. Safety concern: none.

Evidence: the record settles every element the ruling needs — a complete, timestamped chat (4/4 messages timestamped) and a continuous GPS trace from arrival confirmation to cancellation with no hole [F12][F5][F3][NS-1]. No gap.

rejected_claims.reason: Claimed the refund route is NS-2 'and RD-2'; RD-2 is the metered route-deviation formula and does not reach a no-show cancellation fee — the amount ($6.61) and the operative clause are NS-2/NS-7 [F3][F6][NS-2][NS-7]. The relief itself is granted.

Cited RD-6 for the account flag; RD-6 requires an upheld route-deviation case with a positive RD-2 refund, which this file lacks, so the flag rests on NS-2's fake-arrival trigger instead [F5][F1][NS-2][RD-6]. Flag granted on that basis.

D6 likewise invoked RD-6 (and NS-7) for the account flag; as above RD-6 is inapplicable to a no-show file, so only the NS-2 objective trigger supports the referral [F5][F6][NS-2][RD-6]. Substantive relief granted.

D1's framing that the driver 'never confirmed arrival' is imprecise — he did tap 'I'm Here'; NS-1(i) is met, and the fee fails on NS-1(ii)/(iii) (613 m at tap, 0 s inside the radius) [F5][F4][NS-1]. Outcome unchanged.

D5 cited RD-4 as a route-deviation clause against the driver; RD-4 governs traffic excuses for off-route segments and there is no off-route segment in this no-show file. The band-3 readings do not excuse the missed pickup under NS-1 either [F14][F15][F16][NS-1][RD-4]. Outcome unchanged.

C4 referred to congestion as 'not exculpatory under NS-1' — correct in result, but NS-1 contains no traffic-excuse element, so the traffic facts (band 3, no incidents, fair weather) are cited only as background; the fee fails on the positional and duration elements [F14][F16][F17][F5][NS-1]. Outcome unchanged.

events.title: Notices sent to rider and driver
events.body:
RIDER: You were charged a $6.61 cancellation fee after the driver cancelled your ride. We reviewed the record and are refunding that fee in full as a Ryde voucher.

Two things decided this. The driver's "I'm here" tap was made while his GPS showed him about 613 metres from the pickup point, and he never came within the pickup area during the trip. He also didn't wait three minutes at the pickup point before cancelling, and his message saying he was there doesn't match the system record. Your account was not flagged — you were at the Victoria St entrance and asked twice where he was.

The voucher will be added to your Ryde account. No action is needed from you.

DRIVER: We reviewed your no-show cancellation and are not upholding the $6.61 fee. The record shows you tapped "I'm Here" while your GPS put you about 613 metres from the pickup point, and you never entered the pickup area during the trip. You also didn't wait three minutes at the pickup point before cancelling, so the arrival confirmation doesn't stand.

We are removing the fee, so it will not be paid out to you. Your account is also being sent for review because you confirmed arrival while the system showed you outside the pickup area. A reviewer will look at the arrival confirmation, your location history around the pickup, and your recent no-show cases. You'll be contacted about the review's outcome.

actions.detail: account action is never automatic; queued for Ryde review

what_would_change: Had NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both held ((ii) within 200 m of pickup AT THE MOMENT of the arrival confirmation; (iii) stayed at the pickup more than 3 min after the arrival confirmation, until cancelling (NS-1 default: more than 3 min)), the fee would stand and no refund would be due.

claims.assertion: The driver never reached the pickup point: his closest approach was 612 m (F1) and the platform's own record shows driver_arrived_at is null (F4), so he was never at the Victoria St entrance where the rider waited.

The driver tapped 'I'm Here' at 08:16:00 while GPS placed him 613 m from the pickup point, and he spent 0 seconds within 200 m after the tap (F5), so NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail and the $6.61 no-show fee does not stand.

The driver's own message at 08:16 ('I'm here already, please come out', F9) contradicted his position — his stationary period 08:13:10–08:19:30 was 613 m away (F2) — so the '>3 min wait at the pickup' basis for the fee is false.

The driver's claim that traffic prevented him getting closer is not corroborated: Victoria Street was only band 3 (20–29 km/h, F14), no severe band and no incidents were recorded (F16), and weather was fair with 0.0 mm rain (F17); under NS-1 the threshold is positional, not excusable congestion.
Because NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) are not satisfied, the $6.61 charged on the record (F3, F6) must be refunded in full to the rider.

Tapping 'I'm Here' 613 m from the pickup point, then cancelling as a no-show and charging the rider $6.61, is the abuse-of-cancellation/waiting-button conduct for which NS-2 attaches a flag_account referral; the driver's profile shows 2 no-show disputes upheld in 90 days (F19), supporting the referral.

weaknesses: The driver will argue he did press 'I'm Here' and did wait more than 3 minutes before cancelling (F5, F13); the 6 min 20 s stationary period (F2) looks like waiting, and the rider must rely on the 612–613 m distance to show it was not waiting at the pickup point.

The driver's account that Victoria Street was 'jammed solid' (F13) has partial support in the band-3 speed reading on Victoria Street (F14); though band 3 is mid-range and no incidents were recorded (F16), the judge may treat congestion as a mitigating explanation for the missed pickup.

The driver's chat message at 08:16 (F9) is consistent with him believing he had arrived, so the finding may rest on the GPS distance rather than on any intent to deceive; the flag_account request depends on NS-2's objective GPS trigger and on the profile record (F19), which may be argued to concern a different trip.

The chat messages (F8–F11) are timestamped only to the minute, so the exact consent/notification timeline is imprecise, and no message from the rider confirms the driver's presence or absence beyond her statement at 08:17.

claims.assertion: The driver did press "I'm Here", but at 08:16:00 his GPS put him 613 m from the pickup point, never within the arrival radius; the platform's own record, driver_arrived_at, is null, so arrival was never confirmed (F5, F4, F1).
Even taking the tap at face value, the driver stayed inside the pickup radius for 0 seconds after the tap and cancelled at 08:19:30, so the continuous-wait requirement is not met (F5, F3).

The GPS shows the driver stationary 08:13:10–08:19:30 at 613 m from the pickup point while telling the rider at 08:16 "I'm here already, please come out", a location statement the system record contradicts and which therefore cannot ground the no-show fee (F2, F9, F5).

The rider's account is corroborated rather than contradicted: she was at the Victoria St entrance from 08:14, twice asked where the driver was (F8, F10), and her conduct is unrebutted by any system record, so there is no basis to charge her (F8, F10, F6).

The driver's explanation of gridlock is not supported by any RD-4-grade traffic evidence: Victoria Street and North Bridge Road were only band 3 (20–29 km/h) with no incidents recorded anywhere near the route, and weather was fair (F13, F14, F15, F16, F17).

The driver cancelled on a no-show basis yet fails every NS-1 element, so NS-2 governs and the $6.61 charged to the rider (F6) must be returned in full; the same record also supports the additional account flag for tapping "I'm Here" while GPS placed him far outside the pickup area (F5, F19).

weaknesses: The driver's account is not wholly fabricated in form: he did tap "I'm Here" and did wait over three minutes in absolute terms (6 min 20 s stationary, F2, F5), so a sympathetic reader could see a genuine attempt to serve the trip; NS-1 still fails because the wait was at 613 m, not at the pickup point.

The driver's written statement in F13 offers a reason ("Victoria Street was jammed solid") and F14/F15 show moderate traffic (band 3, 20–29 km/h) on those roads, which the other side may cite as partial mitigation for his inability to reach the entrance; F16 (no incidents) and RD-4(a) defeat it as a legal excuse.

F19 shows the driver has 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days, which cuts against any leniency and, combined with the NS-2 account flag, may lead the panel to treat this as repeat conduct rather than an isolated misjudgement.

points.response: Agreed on this point — the tap itself is not the dispute; the GPS record (613 m at tap, via F5) and driver_arrived_at null (F4) are exactly what defeats the fee under NS-1/NS-2.
Conceded; the 0 seconds spent within 200 m after the 08:16:00 tap (F5), with cancellation at 08:19:30 (F3), means NS-1 (iii) fails and no continuous wait at the pickup point exists.
Conceded as framed; the system record (613 m stationary period, F2; 613 m at tap, F5) beats the driver's location claim in F9 and removes any basis for the no-show fee under NS-1.
Conceded; her messages asking where the driver was (F8, F10) are unrebutted by any system record, and nothing in the fare facts (F6) shows a lawful basis for the $6.61 under NS-1.

Conceded, and I go further: band 3 on Victoria Street and North Bridge Road (F14, F15) is moderate traffic, and with no incidents (F16) and fair weather (F17) the driver's gridlock claim in F13 does not reach even RD-4 (b) corroboration, let alone an excuse.

Conceded on the substantive relief: every NS-1 element fails (F5, F3, F4), NS-2 requires full return of the $6.61 (F6), and the flag_account referral is independently supported by the driver's 2 upheld no-show disputes in 90 days (F19) under NS-2/RD-6.
Conceded on the point of fact — my brief already relies on F1 and F4: the closest approach was 612 m and driver_arrived_at is null, so the fee cannot stand on an arrival basis.
Not contested; F5 and F3 are the same facts my claim D2 rests on, and they establish that NS-1 (ii) and (iii) both fail.

Agreed — and I put it more strongly in D3: the 08:16 message "I'm here already, please come out" (F9) is contradicted by the stationary GPS position 613 m from the pickup (F2), so under the system-record rule it cannot support a no-show charge.

Conceded; my own claim D5 uses F14, F16 and F17 against the driver, since RD-4(a) requires a recorded incident on the replaced segment and F16 records none, while band 3 on Victoria Street merely confirms moderate traffic.

The refund conclusion is correct in amount ($6.61, F3, F6) and I ask for refund_full too, but NS-2 is the operative clause — it is the clause that governs when NS-1 (i)(ii)(iii) fail; RD-2 concerns metered route-deviation fares and does not reach a no-show cancellation fee.

I do not resist the flag_account referral, but note NS-2 attaches it on the objective trigger of tapping "I'm Here" while GPS showed him 613 m out (F5), and RD-6 is not the correct route for it here because it requires an upheld route-deviation case with a positive RD-2 refund, which this no-show file has none of.
